//: Synthetic example of config/nodes.json - the node -> role map the
//2: tatbot CLI uses for role gating and --on <node> ssh hops.
//3: Addresses use RFC 5737 documentation ranges; replace every value
//4: with your own deployment. Fields per node: ssh (user@address,
//5: required for --on), roles (list, gates which verbs run here),
//7: differs from the node name), checkout (optional remote repo path;
//7a: null for a node without one), lan (the node's address on the rig
//7b: subnet, where the e-stop relay and bus consumers reach it),
//7c: gpu (optional: the GPU lease's slots, reserve_mib, unified; docs/fleet.md),
//7d: links (optional: the node's address on a direct cable, keyed by the role of
//7e: the node at the other end, never on the rig subnet; the viewer server's
//7f: links carry that node's window off the rig port, docs/vision.md),
//7g: platform (optional: the host's hardware in a word, which the demo viewer's
//7h: load legends show in place of its role), load_via (optional, for a host
//7i: with no checkout: the role whose load monitor reads its CPU and
//7j: temperature over ssh, installing nothing there; docs/vision.md).
//8: Every role the code resolves is held by some node here (the Rust
//9: workspace compiles this map in), laid out as the demo rig: a
//10: workstation plans and serves; the arm host runs the left arm and its
//11: wrist D405; the ROS host runs the drawing stack on the right arm, the
//12: bus router, the viewer, the networked overhead depth camera and the
//13: trackers; a small board relays the one e-stop button to both arms; a
//14: trainer trains. USB cameras are addressed by serial in the vision
//15: config, not listed here; __cameras__ lists networked cameras.
//16: __rig__ names the rig's own subnet and gateway: networked cameras,
//17: arm controllers and every ssh_lan/lan address live in it, and
//18: `tatbot check nodes` holds the vision config, driver profile and
//19: controller YAMLs to it, so renumbering the rig is one edit here.
